verdict: Blackstone's fee business kept growing — management fees rose 6% — but much lower performance allocations left GAAP revenue flat at $3.1B and GAAP profit attributable to shareholders at $662M, while its headline distributable earnings were $1.7B.

kpis.label: Assets under management
kpis.note: $1,368B, +10% YoY; $63B of inflows in the quarter

kpis.label: Distributable earnings (non-GAAP)
kpis.note: $1.32 per share — the headline measure Blackstone manages to

segments.name: Management & advisory fees
segments.note: Steady fees for managing funds — the dependable base of the business, up 6% to about $2.2B. Shown $1M below the reported $2,178M so the pieces add exactly to total revenue (see footer).

segments.name: Incentive fees
segments.note: Fees that depend on fund performance hurdles being met — down from $201M a year ago.

segments.name: Performance allocations
segments.note: Blackstone's share of fund profits (carried interest) on a GAAP basis — down sharply from $781M a year ago, the main reason total revenue was flat.

segments.name: Principal investments
segments.note: Gains on Blackstone's own money invested alongside its funds — a $370M gain vs an $86M loss a year ago.

segments.name: Interest & dividend revenue
segments.note: Interest and dividends earned on cash and investments.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Everything else — a small $12M this quarter.

opex.name: Compensation & benefits
opex.note: Pay and bonuses for staff, including performance pay — down from $1,231M a year ago as performance revenue fell.

opex.name: General, administrative & other
opex.note: Running the firm day to day — offices, technology and professional services.

opex.name: Fund expenses
opex.note: Costs of running the funds themselves.

takeaways.title: The fee base keeps compounding
takeaways.text: Management and advisory fees rose 6% to $2.2B and fee-earning assets reached $990B. Fee Related Earnings — profit from fees alone, a non-GAAP measure — were $1.6B, or $1.26 per share.

takeaways.title: Performance revenue swung down
takeaways.text: GAAP performance allocations fell to $205M from $781M a year ago. That lumpiness is normal for carried interest, but it held total revenue flat even as fees grew.

takeaways.title: Distributable earnings fund the dividend
takeaways.text: Distributable Earnings (non-GAAP) were $1.7B, or $1.32 per share, down 9% YoY. Blackstone declared a $1.12 per-share dividend for the quarter.

oneTimers: Headline non-GAAP measures: Distributable Earnings of $1,716M ($1.32 per share) and Fee Related Earnings of $1,572M ($1.26 per share). This page is built on the GAAP income statement above; the non-GAAP figures use realized performance revenue and exclude unrealized gains and losses.
otherDetail: Other income of $93M, less interest expense of $133M — a net $40M cost. Interest expense is shown inside total expenses in Blackstone's GAAP presentation and is grouped here with other income so the operating lines match how the firm runs the business.
footerNote: The flow uses total GAAP net income of $1,272M; after $610M attributable to noncontrolling interests (mostly holders of Blackstone Holdings partnership units), net income attributable to Blackstone Inc. was $662M ($0.83 per diluted share). Management fees are shown as $2,177M (reported $2,178M) so the revenue pieces add exactly to the $3,063M total — a $1M rounding difference in the release.
